How to Measure Your Bra Size

Follow these simple steps to get accurate measurements for the charts above.

📏 1. Measure Your Underbust (Band)

Wrap a soft tape measure snugly around your ribcage, directly under your bust. Keep the tape level and parallel to the floor. Take the measurement after exhaling normally.

Tip: Round to the nearest even number – e.g., 31" → 32 band.

📐 2. Measure Your Bust (Cup)

Measure around the fullest part of your bust – usually across the nipples. Keep the tape level and don't pull it tight. The tape should sit gently against your skin.

Tip: Take two or three measurements and average them for accuracy.

💡 Formula: Cup Size = Bust Measurement – Band Measurement
1" difference = A cup · 2" = B · 3" = C · 4" = D · 5" = DD · 6" = DDD · 7" = G · and so on.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between US and UK bra sizes?

US and UK bands use the same inch numbers (e.g., 34 is 34 in both). However, cup letters differ from DD upward. US DDD = UK E, US G = UK F, US H = UK FF.

How do I convert EU band size to US?

EU bands are measured in centimetres. Subtract 4 from the US band and multiply by 2.54 to get the EU band. For example, US 34 → (34-4) × 2.54 = 76 cm → EU 75.

What are sister sizes?

Sister sizes have the same cup volume but different band and cup letter combinations. If you go down one band size, go up one cup size. If you go up one band size, go down one cup size. For example, 34C → 32D (tighter band) or 36B (looser band).

How is cup size calculated?

Cup size is the difference between your bust measurement and your band measurement. Each inch of difference equals one cup letter: 1" = A, 2" = B, 3" = C, 4" = D, 5" = DD, 6" = DDD, 7" = G, and so on.

Why is my size different in different brands?

Different brands use different fit models, fabric, and construction. Your size may vary by brand – that's why sister sizing and trying on multiple sizes is recommended.

Does IMRango store my measurements?

No. Everything runs locally in your browser. We do not collect, store, or share any of your personal data or measurements.
